articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom says he was ‘kicked out of’ Game 3 of WNBA Finals
articles.summary: ATLANTA — Enes Kanter Freedom, a former NBA player who has emerged as a vocal opponent of transgender athletes’ participation in women’s sports, said he was...
articles.body:
ATLANTA — Enes Kanter Freedom, a former NBA player who has emerged as a vocal opponent of transgender athletes' participation in women's sports, said he was kicked out of State Farm Arena at Game 3 of the WNBA Finals after declining to use a private suite the Atlanta Dream assigned him to as a safety measure.

Freedom made the assertion in a video posted to X on Wednesday, hours after the Dream released a statement saying Freedom had contacted federal, state and local law enforcement, as well as league officials, before the game to express concern for his safety after announcing his plans to attend.

Moving him to a suite was "intended to address his security concerns and help provide a safe and positive experience for him and other guests," the Dream's statement read.

Additional arena security were assigned to the suite, and at Freedom's request, state police also assigned an officer to protect him.

However, in the video posted on his X account, Freedom can be seen requesting to sit in the seats he had purchased.

Flanked by city police officers as he approaches an entrance to State Farm Arena in the video, Freedom is met by an arena staff member, who is heard telling him, "Before you come in, you have to agree to go to the suite." Freedom responded that he had purchased tickets and "would like to sit in my seat."

After some back and forth, the video cuts to a clip of an officer listing multiple areas Freedom could go to, then saying, "He just can't be here." Freedom then leaves the arena, spreads his arms and says to the camera, "They kicked me out of the game for supporting women."

A Dream spokesperson said Freedom was given an opportunity to return to the arena at any point as long as he was willing to sit in the suite, based on his security concerns.

"I just got kicked out of a @WNBA game for the second time in a row for supporting WOMEN!" Freedom wrote on the X post showing the video. "Let that sink in, AMERICA!"

Opposition to transgender athletes has become a cause célèbre for Freedom, who played 748 games across 11 seasons in the NBA and last appeared in a game in 2022.

Four days before Game 3, Freedom announced he would be in the crowd and name-dropped Dream center Angel Reese and Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams in his social media post.

He previously attended a Chicago Sky game in August wearing a T-shirt that read "WOMAN noun adult human female" and was ejected from his courtside seat after engaging in an in-game verbal exchange with Sky guard Natasha Cloud . The Sky banned Freedom from their home arena after the confrontation, and Freedom filed a lawsuit against the franchise, claiming his First Amendment rights had been violated.

Freedom began posting about threats he received after announcing his plans to attend Wednesday's game.

In the days leading up to the game, neither the WNBA nor the Dream had any official comment on Freedom's attendance, though a plan for a significant uptick in security was expected. The Dream released the statement about Freedom's seating arrangements roughly 40 minutes before Game 3's tipoff.

"The safety and security of our guests and team members is our highest priority," the Dream's statement read.

The teams largely evaded comment on Freedom before the game.

"Obviously, the media has a responsibility in what they choose to cover," Williams said before warmups.

Said Atlanta coach Karl Smesko: "Everyone is here to watch a great basketball game between two great teams, with some of the best players in the world. We're focused on that."

articles.body:
Bandai Namco announced a narrower release window for the upcoming multiplayer-enabled brawler Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3, although it's not too much more specific. Previously, the publisher had stated that the sequel to 2016 fan-favorite would arrive in 2027. Now, it's turned that from a 12-month window into a six-month one, saying that it'll be out in the second half of 2027.

"Today we shared more information about battle customization and PvE missions," producer Masayuki Hirano said. "I wanted to use this opportunity to deliver a message to our fans. Over the past several months, we have continuously revealed new information to all of you and, in return, have received valuable feedback. We are truly grateful for that support. Based on the feedback and survey results we have gathered, we have already held discussions with the development team and announced certain areas where we intend to make improvements in response.

"Dragon Ball Xenoverse is a series that we build together with the players through launch, and throughout its post launch life as well," he continued. "To fully realize our ambitions for both the launch experience and the content we plan to operate and support afterward, the release window is currently set for the latter half of 2027." He concluded by suggesting that the team might stay quiet for a while now, saying, "We may keep you waiting a little longer until our next update, but we are fully committed to making 2027 a great year for Dragon Ball game fans, and we will do everything we can to make that happen."

IGN went hands-on with Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 recently if you'd like to check out our preview impressions . Our first chance to play it was back in June.

articles.title: ‘You can’t…’ – Angel Reese’s ruthless trash talk in dominant Game 3 display goes viral
articles.summary: Angel Reese once again led the way as the Atlanta Dream took Game 3 against the Golden State Valkyries, and she was talking trash while doing it. The Atlanta...
articles.body:
Angel Reese once again led the way as the Atlanta Dream took Game 3 against the Golden State Valkyries, and she was talking trash while doing it.

The Atlanta Dream absolutely dominated the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals, winning by a whopping 26 points. The final score was 97-71 and it almost didn't do justice to how dominant the team was.

Angel Reese followed up her incredible Game 2 performance by picking up right where she left off. She had 21 points, 12 rebounds, three assists, and three steals on the night. It wasn't just her performance that caught the eye, though, it was also the swagger with which she did it.

Angel Reese had multiple instances of talking trash to the Golden State Valkyries which blew up on social media

Reese has been called the biggest trash-talker in the WNBA by the likes of Paige Bueckers. She has suffered at times because of it, her poor performances receive a lot of trolling since she also talks trash. However, when she is on song, the Dream superstar will let her opponents know about it too.

During the second quarter, Reese powered through to the basket for a tough bucket and her reaction after making it went viral.

"You can't guard me," Reese was seen saying to the Valkyries team as she went back down the floor to the other end. In a moment later in the game, she went in on Golden State's Aminata Gueye in another viral clip , saying, "She can't f*** with me."

The Dream find themselves in a commanding position after this latest win in the WNBA Finals. If they are able to see this out, then Angel Reese is absolutely the current favourite for Finals MVP. A couple more performances like this and she will already write her name into the history books. The trash talk is likely to get more intense if that happens.

articles.title: Golden State must address defensive breakdowns after Game 3 loss to Atlanta
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — Golden State has prided itself on its defense all season long. For the second straight WNBA Finals game it failed them.
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Golden State has prided itself on its defense all season long. For the second straight WNBA Finals game it failed them.

The Valkyries dropped Game 3 of the championship series 97-71 on Wednesday night and trail 2-1 in the best-of-seven series. A Golden State team which relies on its league-leading defense was left to explain allowing 97 points while Atlanta shot 49.3% from the field.

"I think this game, they wanted it more than us, and that's not who we are," said guard Tiffany Hayes. "That's not who we've been and that not how we got here."

Golden State had only given up that many points once this season — an overtime loss to Dallas in Game 2 of the first round.

Before Wednesday night's game, Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said she was confident her players would bring better "fight" to Game 3 after the loss to the Dream in Game 2.

"I mean I showed them on film and so they were really like wow like you know it felt like they said that they felt like they're playing hard but then actually watching it on film they're like 'Oh my gosh!' Like it was really eye-opening.

"And they also love to say, you know, film doesn't lie. Like they know it, we know it as coaches. And so they took a lot of accountability. So they were just very like, OK, we got it."

Instead, the Valkyries missed their first eight shots and never led.

Nakase said she her team was "just undisciplined" on defense and questioned if players were struggling with the defensive plan. Nakase said if "something is being a little bit unclear, then that's all of me."

"We weren't in our shifts consistently," Nakase said. "We weren't communicating. We were kind of just late on certain rotations, which was just uncharacteristic."

Gabby Williams scored 15 points but made only 5 of 18 shots from the field. Cecilia Zandalasini scored 13 points while making four of six 3-pointers. No other starter scored until the final period, though Hayes had 14 points and Janelle Salaun scored 13 points off the bench.

Williams said if the Valkyries can fix their defense better offense will follow.

"I think sometimes shots don't fall," Williams said. "You know, we don't want to make it about offense. They scored what, 97? ... We have to get back to what works for us. We have to just go back to our defense and not what our offense is going to be."

Veronica Burton, who averaged 12.2 points while starting every game in the regular season, made only 1 of 7 shots for three points.

"We had a couple lull moments throughout the game," Burton said. "Obviously that third quarter, the comeback, we punched first and then it gets away from us. I think that's kind of where it happened the most. They go on runs, and we weren't able to get them back."

Nakase was smiling as she entered the postgame interview room and said she remains confidence in the Valkyries' chances.

"I feel like this is just a long series," Nakase said. "We've been down before. We've come back from games where we've been down and so now we just wanna just put it as a longer series. ... So it's just a longer series if you guys think about it. So we're resilient. We've done it before. They know that."

articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream have taken control of the WNBA Finals after crushing the Golden State Valkyries, 97-71, in Game 3 at State Farm Arena on Wednesday and gaining the upper hand, 2-1, in the best-of-seven series.

The Dream carried a six-point advantage at halftime before blowing the game open in the third quarter. They never looked back, leading by as much as 26 points.

While coach Karl Smesko acknowledged their strong performance, he also issued a stern reminder to his players.

"I like the energy we played with, even after getting off to a little slow start in the second half. You guys on your own regrouped, figured it out, and made all the plays," said Smesko in the video posted by USA Sports.

"We should be happy with the way we competed today. But we have to be cognizant that it is only halfway done. The job is only halfway done. There's more work to be done, and we're going to do it."

Angel Reese was phenomenal anew, tallying 21 points, 12 rebounds, three assists, and three steals. Reese set the tone early, including talking smack to the Valkyries in the first quarter .

Rhyne Howard bounced back from her meager output in Game 2, tallying 16 points, four rebounds, four assists, and five steals.

Naz Hillmon contributed 15 points and two rebounds, while Isobel Borlase had 12 points and five rebounds.

The Dream have no time to be overcomplacent, especially against the Valkyries, who have shown throughout their inspired run that they can overcome tall obstacles, including dethroning the Las Vegas Aces.

articles.title: Angel Reese (again), Valkyries' turnovers among WNBA Finals winners and losers
articles.summary: The Dream took a 2-1 lead in the 2026 WNBA Finals following a 95-71 win over the Golden State Valkyries. Here are the winners and losers.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream are halfway to their first WNBA championship.

The Dream took a 2-1 lead in the 2026 WNBA Finals following a 95-71 win over the Golden State Valkyries during Game 3 at State Farm Arena on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

Atlanta was led by Angel Reese who had 21 points, 12 rebounds and three steals. Rhyne Howard had 16 points and five steals. Naz Hillmon had 15 points and Jordin Canada 10 points and eight assists.

"Time to take over. Do whatever it takes to win," Reese said postgame. "I said this game, I don't want to have to say, 'Give me the ball.' Everybody was just playing together. It's fun when you win and you play with a great group.

The Valkyries didn't register a field goal until the 4:38 mark of the first uqarter when center-forward Aminata Gueye hit a hook shot off the glass. They shot 35% from the field, compared to 49% from the Dream.

Here are the winners and losers from Game 3 of the WNBA Finals:

Celebrities show up in style for an unforgettable WNBA Finals

Not to sound like a broken record, but Dream forward Angel Reese recorded another double-double in the Finals.

After a 30-point, 16-rebound double-double in Game 2, Reese finished with 21 points and 12 rebounds in Game 3 to mark her third consecutive double-double in the WNBA Finals. With her performance, Reese becomes the first player in WNBA Finals history to record three straight double-doubles.

Let's not forget that this is the first postseason appearance of Reese's budding career.

"When you can do it at the highest level, this is what I live for," said Reese, who added three assists and three steals in the win. "This is what the offseason is for. I put the work in for this moment and I'm just happy I can lead the team to a win and we're feeling good going into (Game 4 on) Saturday."

For all of the contributions the city of Atlanta has made to music, film and entertainment, it's about time its residents get to enjoy some WNBA success.

Since it was established as an expansion franchise in 2008, the Atlanta Dream hadn't won a Finals gamer until Angel Reese took over in Game 2 Monday night. Now, the franchise is two wins away from its first championship.

Atlanta's commanding victory was enjoyed by a sellout crowd at State Farm arena, which was filled with celebrities. From rapper 2 Chainz to actress Kerry Washington, the stars were out and enjoying history in the making while swag surfing among the fans. It surely a win for the culture in the city. Just ask rapper Ludacris , who sat courtside with his daughters and called the Dream's emergence a dream come true.

After setting a WNBA Finals record with six steals in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals, Howard followed up that performance with five steals in the Dream's Game 3 blowout win. With her master thievery, Howard becomes the first player in WNBA Finals history to record five or more steals in consecutive games.

More importantly, Howard appeared to break out of her shooting slump with 16 points, shooting 4-of-11 from the field, 1-of-2 from the 3-point line and 7-of-10 from the free-throw line to record her highest scoring game across the 2026 WNBA Finals series.

She entered Wednesday's matchup with the mindset to "just be better."

"Even this (game) wasn't up to my liking," Howard said in her postgame interview. "I got to have an impact on that side of the floor. There's no doubt about it. I know that I haven't necessarily been up to par, but today I had a couple more shots and I continue to play defense."

Howard has done a little bit of everything for the Dream, despite struggling offensively. She added four rebounds and four assists to her stat line.

"(Rhyne Howard), she came up big with her five steals," Angel Reese said. "I think everybody contributed."

The Golden State Valkyries are praised for being a defensive team but the Atlanta Dream deserve just as much recognition for their defensive prowess. The Dream felt like they should be up 3-0 because each game they've stifled the Valkyries. Game 3 was no different.

Atlanta held Golden State to 35% shooting, including forcing 17 turnovers, scoring 22 points off those takeaways. Angel Reese nabbed three steals, while Rhyne Howard led the team with five steals.

The Dream's defense was effective early and often. Atlanta held the Valkyries to 0 points through opening 5 minutes, 22 seconds of the game.

Atlanta couldn't be stopped in the paint. Reese had another double-double going for 21 points, 12 rebounds on an efficient 7-for-12 shooting. She helped fuel the Dream's domination in the paint, going right at the Valkyries defenders off the dribble, coast-to-coast on fastbreaks or sealing in the post and making a strong move.

Rhyne Howard made a couple of circus shots driving to the basket. And Jordin Canada got to the lane at will, whether she finished with a layup or found the open teammate.

The Dream outscored the Valkyries in the paint, 44-20.

WNBA Finals: Atlanta Dream vs. Golden State Valkyries battle in Game 3

Valkyries' Gabby Williams shooting struggles continue

The Dream have made things difficult for the Valkyries, especially their leading scorer Gabby Williams, who was Golden State's leading scoring in Game 3 with 15 points on 5-for-18 shooting. Williams went into a facilitating mode, racking up eight assists because her shot just wasn't falling.

Atlanta has been all over Williams throughout the entire series. In Game 2, Williams shot 3-for-15. Her best game was Game 1, when she went 8-for-22 from the field. Throughout the season, when Williams struggled another one of her teammates would step up.

It hasn't happened in the WNBA. The Dream has held Golden State to under 35% shooting this series.

The Golden State Valkyries are known for their depth, with the highest-scoring bench in the regular season. The Valkyries' reserves showed up big in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals, but the team's starters were missing in action.

Golden State's starters were collectively held to three points in the first quarter. By halftime, the Valkyries' starting lineup had accumulated 11 points.

The starting unit — made up of Gabby Williams (15 pts), Cecilia Zandalasini (13 pts), Veronica Burton (three points, four assists), Kiah Stokes (two points, three blocks) and Kayla Thornton (zero points) — finished with 33 total points.

"Sometimes shots don't fall," said Williams, who is shooting 29.1% from the field and 28% from the 3-point line across three Finals games. "We don't want to make it about offense. They scored 97 (points). We have no chance. We have to just go back to our defense and that will get our offense going."

The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream's elite defenses are causing chaos and turnovers at a high rate. Both teams have struggled to hold on to the ball. However, Golden State's ball security is becoming alarming.

For the third straight game, Golden State averaged double-digit turnovers. And for the second straight game, there have 15 or more giveaways. In Game 2, there was 19 turnovers for 24 points. In Game 3, Atlanta scored 22 points off 17 Valkyries turnovers. If Golden State wants a chance at keeping up with Atlanta, it has to be more mindful about conceding points off turnovers while also returning the favor and forcing the Dream to also give up the ball.

"I think (this is) all about us being undisciplined. We don't really lose the ball. So, again, very uncharacteristic of us," Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes said postgame. "We have to get back to who we are. (If) they bring some pressure, we got to stay together. We gotta not get flustered, just giving the ball up. So I think it's us that has to make some adjustments."

Following the Dream's Game 2 win Monday night, Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase let out an exasperated "Girl! What did I say?" after a reporter didn't take a nod to the team's defensive identity as an answer to a question about why scoring has been such a struggle in the series. "We are a defensive-minded team," Nakase emphasized at the time. But after scoring 15 points or less in the first and fourth quarters of Wednesday's Game 3, it's clear the Valkyries need to shift their focus to making some more buckets.Golden State has been held under 35% shooting in all three games of the series.

articles.title: 'We Were Working on a Great Game' — Former Mass Effect 5 Writers Speak Out After EA Shuts Down BioWare
articles.summary: `Former writers for the now-canceled Mass Effect 5 are speaking out on social media following news that BioWare, a beloved studio with more than 30 years of games under its belt, was shuttered by EA earlier today.
articles.body:
Former writers for the now-canceled Mass Effect 5 are speaking out on social media following news that BioWare, a beloved studio with more than 30 years of games under its belt, was shuttered by EA earlier today.

EA announced the news somewhat unceremoniously in a single paragraph tucked within a lengthy open letter on October 21, 2026. “As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly,” the statement reads.

It’s safe to say that gamers were gutted by this announcement — as were the staff impacted by the closure, as we’ve now seen several writers who worked on Mass Effect 5 begin to discuss the situation online.

11 Mass Effect Characters and Moments the TV Show Needs to Be a Hit

On Twitter/X, New York Times bestselling author Catherynne M. Valente responded to a post wherein a user said, “A game industry that cannot figure out how to make a sequel to the literal best game of all time is a game industry that is fundamentally broken,” speaking on the BioWare closure.

“We did figure it out. We were working on a great game. Just saying,” Valente retorted . In response to a different commenter, she revealed that she hadn’t contributed to Dragon Age: The Veilguard, Mass Effect: Andromeda, or Anthem, clarifying that she is “not, in fact, the personification of BioWare."

Award-winning science fiction writer Derek Künsken also published a lengthy thread discussing his time working on Mass Effect 5 — a game that, most likely, we’ll never get to see. Künsken said he’d been contributing to the title “on and off” over the last five years, and said he’s only now allowed to speak about it given that the company behind the project is now nonexistent.

“Over the coming weeks, I'll get more clarity on what I can say about what I did and saw and learned. I hope it's more than nothing — what we were cooking was really cool,” he said. He went on to reveal that he’d worked with Valente on pitching “story, character, lore, and sci-fi wonder for this next chapter of the Mass Effect world,” calling it “the most energizing, in-the-zone collaboration I've ever had.”

For now, fans are left wondering what could have been, while equally hopeful that somehow, some way, EA might sell off BioWare’s IPs to another studio rather than letting them languish. Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah is expressing some caution around this particular idea, though he did theorize that it’s a bit more likely now, given that EA is possibly looking to offset its massive debt incurred by its eye-watering $55 billion acquisition to a private investment group earlier this year.

Oh well; at least we have the Prime Video series to look forward to, which was revealed to still be in active development in an exclusive statement to IGN.

In a world where market price has become the new MSRP for the Pokémon Trading Card Game , it can be hard to consider the possibility of securing the hottest ETBs out there right now for a whole lot less.

Thankfully, there's been a couple of recent wins for trainers this week, with retailers like Best Buy and Amazon prioritising invite systems to ensure the rarest sets are being distributed fairly.

Now, Amazon is selling the Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Boxes for just $59.99 ... if you can secure an invite to buy. That's a big if, but it's a whole lot better than paying the $120+ market price you'd find at TCGplayer or other resellers.

Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box

While it can be frustrating for anyone who simply wants to purchase these without jumping through hoops, it does somewhat even the playing field and at least allows a select number of trainers to buy without the stress of short drop windows.

Plus, in my view, this system does allow even more people to get their hold on cards to open up, collect, and use, rather than folk who just want to pick up a few ETBs to sell on again.

As I mentioned, Best Buy has done something similar with the elusive and extremely rare Pokémon TCG: Prismatic Evolutions ETBs , selling those for just $49.99 to those who are invited to purchase.

Pokémon TCG: Prismatic Evolutions Elite Trainer Box

In the same way as Amazon’s Pokémon invites go out, your invite request will be kept on Best Buy’s system to be in consideration for the next (or future) stock drops the retailer gets for this particular ETB — before randomly selecting who amongst those requesters actually get an invite.

If you do get selected, of which you’ll be notified by email, you’ll have 24 hours to purchase your Prismatic Evolutions ETB before said invite expires. In light of that fairly narrow window, that’s also why Best Buy advises you to download and use the Best Buy app as well, so you can get real-time alert notifications.

Whilst this all means requesting an invite doesn’t guarantee you’ll get selected this time, you’ll at least stay on the list for any future restocks, too, so you don’t need to request one again each time. That counts for both Amazon, and Best Buy as well.

For now, to give you an idea of where the dust is settling on the 30th anniversary set, we’ve also recently pulled the median market prices per TCGplayer for the top 10 highest-value cards in the set , so you know what to look out for when ripping packs. See those just below, and good luck!

articles.summary: Burguer Shot aparecía en el Kaseya Center, el estadio de los Miami Heat
articles.body: Se acerca el día, el día más esperado de la década en el sector de los videojuegos. Y es que el 19 de noviembre llegará a nuestras consolas el GTA 6, el juego que ahora mismo capta toda la atención, además de por la expectación que genera en los jugadores, porque la marca de Grand Theft Auto es tan grade que trasciende más allá de las pantallas como estamos viendo últimamente en la ciudad de Miami. Y es que Rockstar está llevando a cabo una estrategia de marketing digna de un lanzamiento como este en Miami, la ciudad en la que se basa el GTA 6 para desarrollar su historia. El último ejemplo tiene que ver con Burguer Shot, la franquicia de hamburguesería ficticia que aparece en toda la saga de Grand Theft Auto. Esta madrugada se celebraba en Miami el partido inaugural de la temporada de los Heat de la NBA en el Kaseya Center entre el equipo local y los Minnesota Timberwolves. articles.title: Street Fighter Was Never Going to Be a Dark, Grounded Batman Begins-Style Movie, Director Insists — the Studio Wanted Silliness and Absurdity
articles.summary: Street Fighter is the number one movie in North America, but it’s sparked much debate about its goofy tone. Some fans of Capcom’s fighting game franchise had wanted something darker and more grounded than what they got, but according to the movie’s director, that was never on the cards.
articles.body:
Street Fighter is the number one movie in North America, but it’s sparked much debate about its goofy tone. Some fans of Capcom’s fighting game franchise had wanted something darker and more grounded than what they got, but according to the movie’s director, that was never on the cards.

Director Kitao Sakurai told The Hollywood Reporter that the studio behind the movie, Legendary, wanted something that he had become known for through the likes of The Eric Andre Show and Bad Trip: absurdity.

Sakurai said he'd never have got the job as writer and director if he had he pitched Legendary 'the Batman Begins of Street Fighter movies.'

“We, for sure, wouldn’t be sitting here right now,” he said. “The assignment specifically came about because of the spiritual nature of Street Fighter and the fact that it’s not gory. There’s a silliness to it, and there’s an absurdity to the world and the characters and how they interact. [Producer] Cale Boyter at Legendary really held the torch for this vision of Street Fighter that had a gonzo energy to it. I also love comedy and craziness and energy.

“Sometimes things don’t necessarily need to make sense for you to lean in and love them. That was a big lesson from The Eric Andre Show. There’s a quote from a famous stand-up comic who says that if you do a 60-minute stand-up special, not every minute needs to be hilarious and funny, but every minute needs to be interesting. So there can be elements that are so ridiculous they might not track narratively or make sense conceptually, but because they’re part of an overall energy and feeling, they fit. So I kept that in mind when I was developing this film.”

The result is a film that was panned by critics but audiences are enjoying. Street Fighter has a 41% rating on Rotten Tomatoes ’ Tomatometer, and a 78% rating on its Popcornmeter, highlighting this divide. IGN’s Street Fighter review returned a 6/10. We said: “Street Fighter benefits from a very enthusiastic cast and an anarchic spirit, but Kitao Sakurai’s adaptation of the Capcom games struggles to focus all that energy into a well-told story.”

The question for Legendary and for Sakurai is, will Street Fighter do well enough to get a sequel? The movie leaves the door open to a follow-up with various teases for where it might go. But is anything in the works? Sakurai kept his cards close to his chest.

“It’s something we’re thinking about,” he said. “We haven’t put pen to paper. This is a story that we all love, and I would love to tell more of it. I think everybody in the cast had such an incredible time, so there’s certainly interest in it. But there’s nothing set in stone or any concrete plans.”

We've got plenty more on Street Fighter while you wait to find out what's next, including its opening weekend box office , why we think it makes a mistake that Mortal Kombat already learned from , and our breakdown of its ending .

articles.title: Microsoft’s next-generation Xbox may launch after 2028: Here is how much it may cost
articles.summary: Gamers must brace for expensive computing hardware over the next few years, specifically for flagship consoles.
articles.body: Gamers must brace for expensive computing hardware over the next few years, specifically for flagship consoles. According to a report by Fortune, internal Microsoft estimates project that the next-generation Xbox could cost between $1,200 and $1,800. On top of the potential pricing spike, the system may not hit store shelves until 2028. Notably, at an $1,800 ceiling, the upcoming console would cost nearly four times as much as its predecessor did at launch. This comes as industry rumours suggest Sony’s anticipated PlayStation 6 could also climb upwards of $1,000.New leadership and hardware realitiesThe price and launch timeline come at a time when Microsoft’s gaming division is undergoing a period of major restructuring, marked by additional workforce layoffs and the appointment of Asha Sharma as the new chief executive officer (CEO) of Xbox. Sharma has laid out targets for the brand, including scaling Xbox into a billion-player-a-day platform.Meanwhile, persistent global hardware inflation is challenging the standard business model. Microsoft itself believes it’s no longer feasible to develop a high-performance machine that boasts flagship capabilities and fits in the traditional consumer-friendly price tags.For players seeking a more wallet-friendly entry point, Microsoft may offer an alternative ahead of its flagship living-room hardware. Sharma told Fortune that an official next-generation Xbox handheld is planned for release in time for the holiday 2027 shopping season.While launching the portable device in late 2027 gives global component volatility some breathing room, major technology manufacturers widely anticipate that industry-wide memory shortages will linger well into 2028.What is Microsoft's Project ‘Xbox Helix’The persistent supply snags present a major hurdle for the upcoming home console, codenamed Xbox Helix. Microsoft will need to lock down final architectural choices and commit to massive component orders ahead of high-volume mass production – an operational milestone anticipated for late 2027 or early 2028. The surging costs of raw silicon, advanced memory modules and specialised fabrication account directly for the eye-watering estimates.While cutting-edge exclusives and next-generation processing muscle will inevitably attract dedicated early adopters, the prospect of a console priced past $1,500 introduces steep commercial risks.You use AI every day. articles.title: Golden State Valkyries couldn’t meet the moment again. Can they recover in the WNBA Finals?
articles.summary: ATLANTA — The last refuge of a desperate coach is the technical foul. Tantrum size depends on the circumstances. But it’s always at least enough to earn the...
articles.body:
ATLANTA — The last refuge of a desperate coach is the technical foul. Tantrum size depends on the circumstances. But it's always at least enough to earn the official reprimand and, most important, it's usually an attempt to throw both hands into the mud and yank out a team sinking fast. A way to wring something, anything, out of a whole lot of nothing.

See me? The one yelling a lot over here? Can you guys maybe try to do the basketball player version of that, out there on the floor?

This was Natalie Nakase, up to her shoulders in the mire on Wednesday night and looking for anything to hold on to. Or for any signs of sustained vitality from her club in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals. A virile protest of an offensive foul call, a slap on the wrist from a referee, and an impassioned huddle with her Golden State Valkyries on the sideline. It didn't work. Add it to the increasingly ominous list.

There aren't many answers left when you make promises you don't keep, which is the story of a 97-71 loss to the Atlanta Dream that reads like a draft of an obituary. This would be the "best fight" the Valkyries had shown all season, their head coach announced before the game. Guaranteed. They would not get outworked and outpunched again this series. Cross her heart.

It wasn't anywhere in the same universe as enough. The offense no-showed to start, when any hint of effectiveness could've helped mute a red-hot sellout crowd of 17,099. When the Valkyries at last discovered some shooting, it was at the expense of its effectiveness on the defensive end. In a blink, Golden State looked fatally exposed. Too limited. Too binary. A team that can do only one thing well at once, flailing against an opponent that figured out how to do whatever it wants.

"Yeah, sometimes promises aren't kept," Nakase mused after the game.

"I mean, the beauty of this is the openness they had right after the game of being super coachable and wanting information. I don't ever (say) they don't want it, or that they don't want to fight. How do we make sure we can do it all together? There's sometimes individual punches, some people with great spurts, and some people have great energy. It's like, well, how can we do it all together? That's on me. The will is there. The want-to is there. But the fight together, I'm missing the piece of putting it together."

When you make everything a life-or-death situation, the old coaching saying goes, you run into problems. For one thing, you'll be dead a lot.

But that was the setup Wednesday. That was the line the coach drew. Nakase put the night in unequivocal terms. Her team couldn't meet the demand of the moment, and got bludgeoned. So what now? How many times can you try to set off the alarms, before you realize all the batteries are dead?

"This game, they wanted it more than us," Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes said. "That's not who we are. That's not who we've been. That's not how we got here."

It's a go-to postgame appraisal, but in this situation it's an indictment, to begin with. If the Valkyries don't have that, they don't have much.

Maybe more startling — if that's a 14-year-veteran telling the truth, more than dipping into the answers that get you out of a post-loss news conference as efficiently as possible — it's also a contradiction. Nakase walked into the same room a few minutes later and said her team played as hard as it could. She said that in these situations, her team is resilient, and typically comes together even tighter.

But Game 3 was already one of those situations. Resilience and togetherness were already supposed to be on the menu. Instead, Golden State never held a lead on Wednesday. Afterward, Nakase, Hayes and Gabby Williams all used some form of the word "undisciplined" as they reflected on what happened, and what didn't.

"It's very uncharacteristic of us," Hayes said.

It's very, very weird to think of the Golden State Valkyries not being on the same page. That's sort of the premise of them. They understand the plan, surrender to their roles in it and execute with precision. It can be aesthetically challenging at times, but that's fine. As long as the string tying the group together doesn't have much give.

The Dream have done an excellent job of pulling on the loose ends for the last two games, due to coach Karl Smesko pushing buttons with more success than Nakase and Angel Reese effectively out-wanting everyone else on the floor. "In my heart, I'm not letting you take this from us," Reese declared after a 21-point, 12-rebound effort that also featured three steals and two 3-pointers. "I think it becomes contagious within the team. They feel that confidence, too."

But when things unraveled a bit for the Dream in Game 3, early in the second half, it wasn't willpower or white-board wizardry that tightened them up. As Smesko put it: His players simply came together and decided to clean it up. They huddled. They regrouped. They made winning plays with composure, shot 49 percent against the best defense in the WNBA and blew their opponents out of the gym.

That's supposed to be the Valkyries. Or at least it's also supposed to be them.

But they've lost themselves a bit right now, at a time of the year when you don't want to start looking for what's missing.

There will be double-doses of film here over the next two days anyway — as a team and as individuals, per Nakase — because you stay on the hunt until told otherwise. And maybe the reemergence of Janelle Salaün as an offensive threat, for one example, is a harbinger instead of a blip. Golden State won the first game of this series because it's good enough to win games in the WNBA Finals. It can win more of them.

The Valkyries contingent was right to say it's a long series. They just sounded a little somber when they said it.

"We're resilient," Nakase said. "We've done it before. They know that. Again, it's on my shoulders. I gotta figure out maybe a couple different schemes that could be a little more aggressive. I could be a little more clear, make sure we're fighting with the right units. This is on me."

Full marks for the Valkyries coach taking ownership. It's what a good coach does.

It's also what any coach says after she's done everything else she can think of, and her team is still wondering where it lost its footing in the middle of the fall.

Atlanta Dream, Golden State Valkyries, WNBA

articles.title: Resident Evil Developer Capcom Issues Phishing Warning After Data Breach Hits Over 11 Million Customer Accounts
articles.summary: Capcom has disclosed a data breach of its online membership service affecting over 11 million customer accounts, warning gamers to brace themselves for potential phishing attempts.
articles.body:
Capcom has disclosed a data breach of its online membership service affecting over 11 million customer accounts, warning gamers to brace themselves for potential phishing attempts.

The Resident Evil, Monster Hunter, and Street Fighter developer said customer information associated with Capcom ID was accessed by a third-party on October 19. 11.7 million email address records were affected globally, exposing date and time of account creation, date and time of last login, number of logins, and the client IP address used during last login.

Of these, 43 records of date of birth, gender, country/region, and nickname were affected, and 196 accounts saw unauthorized changes to their Capcom ID login passwords. Capcom said the passwords associated with these accounts have already been reset, as it “continues to investigate the scope of any impact resulting from this incident.”

While the data breach is damaging, Capcom insisted passwords customers created themselves were not leaked, and credit card information was not included among the affected information. It does not expect its video games to be affected.

Capcom said it reported the incident to the Osaka Prefectural Police and Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission. It told customers they may continue to use the email addresses registered with Capcom ID, but warned that there is the possibility that the affected information could be misused to send fraudulent emails.

“If you receive any suspicious email or message, please exercise caution and refrain from accessing any URLs contained therein or opening any attached files,” Capcom advised.

Capcom didn’t go into detail on how it was hacked, but said it had completed emergency response measures and had “identified and addressed the attack method involved in this incident.”

“Capcom takes this matter extremely seriously and will continue its detailed investigation,” the company concluded.

“Based on the findings of the investigation, it will implement measures to prevent recurrence and further strengthen its information security framework. Should any additional facts requiring disclosure be identified, Capcom will promptly provide updates through the company’s official website and other appropriate channels.

“Capcom would once again like to express its sincere apologies to its customers and all other stakeholders.”

articles.title: 'Regions Are Cheating and We Need to Address It' — Wardogs Dev Says Region Locking Is About 'Protecting the Largest Amount of Players'
articles.summary: Bulkhead is rolling out region locking in Wardogs to, in the studio's words, protect "the largest amount of players from an influx of regions that are more prone to cheating." However, legitimate players in Asia have raised concerns, and cross-region players have criticized the developer for blocked from joining their friends.
articles.body:
Bulkhead is rolling out region locking in multiplayer first-person shooter Wardogs to, in the studio's words, protect "the largest amount of players from an influx of regions that are more prone to cheating." However, legitimate players in Asia have raised concerns, and cross-region players have criticized the developer for blocked from joining their friends.

The region lock is done by limiting the maximum ping — the player’s connection with the server — to 175. On paper, this is a fair, non-discriminatory way to stop players from distant regions from entering games with an unstable connection. According to Bulkhead, this would cut down on cheating, too.

“We have decided [to protect] the largest amount of players from an influx of regions that are more prone to cheating,” Bulkhead tweeted . “It’s disappointing for us to have to put these divisions in place with social experience being such a core focus of Wardogs, but we must prioritize the largest group of players over the minority.

“Region locking is in progress on the backend, but is more than a switch to make a meaningful impact to the desired effect. We’re sorry we let it get to this point that we are forced to make this decision, but we felt that giving certain regions the opportunity to prevail was the right move. Unfortunately, it has not panned out as we’d hoped and we’ll be getting stricter on cross pollination of regions.”

Some players are already asking for refunds after being blocked from being able to play with their international friends. “As an American with Australian friends this is a bulls**t change,” said one player . “Why don’t we just call a spade a spade and stop access solely from China?”

"Oh that's cool, I'll be getting a refund then," another player said . "F**k this rugpull bulls**t. I didn't buy Wardogs to play some hardcore shooter, I got it to play with my mates, and there was no bulls**t ping limit. Nor will this actually stop cheaters."

“What you clearly should be doing is strengthening the anti-cheat mode, yet the measure you've taken is to outright ban us Asian players,” said another player . “We have to endure discrimination against Asians: a normal kill on a player gets flagged as a high-ping player [and is] instantly labeled a ‘Chinese cheater’ in the public channel.

“This comes from a group of people who don't bother verifying anything and jump straight to accusations, stuffing their slanders with all sorts of profanity and personal attacks. And yet, we still choose to keep playing your game under all these negative effects, even helping to dispel rumors for fellow Asians ourselves, instead of abandoning it.”

There are dozens of posts with similar sentiment in the replies to the Wardogs announcement. The general vibe seems to be that this is a poor change that will negatively impact players across all regions, instead of dealing with the core issue of identifying and quickly banning cheaters.

In response to a YouTuber backing the company decision, Wardogs CEO Joe Brammer said the team is working on solutions for global players. “Appreciate that we’re harming a % of players to protect the larger,” he said. “We will find a solution, this issue is bigger than Wardogs though… We’re working on solutions for global players… Sucks.”

Brammer went on to say the current ping-based solution is a quick fix, "not a permanent solution."

"That is coming but takes longer than it needs to be," he continued. "It’s not as simple as 'flip a switch'... tracking where people are actually based is not straight forward (VPN etc etc)."

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: Playasia Store Pulled Offline After Weeks of 'Increasingly Sophisticated and Relentless Attacks'
articles.summary: Hong Kong-based online retail store Playasia has been forced to temporarily shut down after weeks of aggressive cyberattacks, the company has claimed.
articles.body:
Hong Kong-based online retail store Playasia was forced to temporarily shut down after weeks of aggressive cyberattacks, the company has claimed. The news was announced on X / Twitter via a message from company CEO Jan Neuhäußer.

“After weeks of increasingly sophisticated and relentless attacks against us and several of our trusted partners, we made the decision to go dark while we complete a full security audit and harden our systems,” the CEO said .

“This is not a step we take lightly. Playasia has been our home, and your home, for nearly 24 years, and the thought of stepping away even for a short while breaks my heart.”

According to the company, the attacks aren’t random and Playasia is listed as a target alongside thousands of other digital-first companies. “This is a coordinated, systemic campaign, not something aimed only at Playasia,” Neuhäußer continued.

“Watching our team work around the clock, exhausted but still fighting to protect what we have built together, has brought me to tears more than once. Many of them have families who depend on them. I have my own. The passion that has driven this community of gamers serving fellow gamers for over two decades is something we will not let anyone take from us.

“We have reported everything to the relevant authorities and cybercrime units worldwide and continue to share every detail that can help them pursue those responsible. We are doing everything in our power to protect our customers, our partners, and our people.

“Your support over the years has meant more than I know how to say. Please stay tuned for updates on our social channels and here.”

Playasia was founded in 2002 and is popular for its range of region-exclusive or Asian-English versions of video games, toys, and collectibles. This comes in the middle of what security professionals are calling Black October, during which a critical flaw was found in PHP, a scripting language affecting 70% of websites.

“Effective Immediately, all organizations using PHP for their systems are advised to be prepared for an update addressing two critical vulnerabilities,” said the NSA cyber security division. “PHP is widely used for web applications. These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database. If an immediate update is not feasible, it is recommend (sic) that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.”

There is no evidence to suggest the Playasia shutdown is linked to the new vulnerability, which has seen swarms of AI agents hacking the internet, but it’s certainly a dark time for internet security.

articles.title: Amazon Has a Decent Sale on PS5 Games in the Run Up to Black Friday
articles.summary: Amazon has a decent sale on PS5 games right now in the lead-up to Black Friday sales, offering discounts on Resident Evil Requiem, Borderlands 4, and more.
articles.body:
When it comes to finding big discounts on physical video games, Black Friday is the time to watch out for . This sale event usually doesn't start up until November, but Amazon's been sneaking in some offers before then for eager shoppers to check out. Already the retailer has a solid selection of PS5 game deals available to look through, including a record-low price on Borderlands 4 and Resident Evil Requiem back to its lowest price point .

Resident Evil Requiem - Amazon Exclusive Edition

Final Fantasy VII Rebirth - Exclusive Amazon Edition

Requiem's deal price is actually a return to the price we saw during Amazon's recent October Prime Day sale event , which marked a full $20 discount off its MSRP. In a similar position is Star Wars Zero Company , which is just pennies away from its Prime Day price at the retailer, saving you just over $10 compared to paying its full cost.

Final Fantasy VII Rebirth is another that caught our eye - initially as part of the Square Enix sale that popped up at Amazon recently - that's also returned to its lowest price point at Amazon. Right now it's available for just $20, which is a steal in comparison to its launch price of $70. And with Final Fantasy VII Revelation coming out next year, this is a perfect time to play it if you haven't yet.

Another standout game on sale right now is Pragmata , which is also back down to its lowest point at the retailer. It did dip to $39.99 during the most recent October Prime Day sale at Amazon, but that was exclusive to Prime members. For everyday shoppers, this is still a nice discount to jump on for one of our favorite games of the year so far .

Some other new releases from this year that are also on sale at Amazon are Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy and Mouse: P.I. For Hire . Both of these have dropped to new lows at the retailer, so it's a great time to pick them up if they've been on your wishlist. There's much more to check out alongside everything I've mentioned, too. Have a look through our favorite deals above, and we'll be keeping an eye out for even more early PS5 game deals as we inch closer to November.
